definitions.explanation: Suffix attached to a number, yen amount, or percentage to express a price reduction. The rendaku form of {引|ひ}き (pulling, subtracting).

examples.japanese: {二|に}{割|わり}{引|び}きで{買|か}った。
{五百|ごひゃく}{円|えん}{引|び}きのクーポンを{使|つか}った。
{会員|かいいん}は{全|ぜん}{商品|しょうひん}が{一|いっ}{割|わり}{引|び}きで{購入|こうにゅう}できる。
examples.english: Members can purchase all items at 10% off.

notes:
Voiced form (rendaku) of {引|ひ}き. Attaches to a number expressing how much is taken off a price.

COMPOUNDS:
- {一|いっ}{割|わり}{引|び}き: 10% off
- {半|はん}{額|がく}{引|び}き: half-price off (more often just {半額|はんがく})
- {千|せん}{円|えん}{引|び}き: 1,000 yen off
- {学割|がくわり}{引|び}き: student discount

USAGE:
For percentages, Japanese normally uses {割|わり} (= 10%): {三割引|さんわりびき} (30% off). For yen amounts, the figure plus {円|えん} attaches directly: {三百|さんびゃく}{円|えん}{引|び}き. Often appears on store signs and coupons.
